title: PyTorch: An Imperative Style, High-Performance Deep Learning Library
authors: A. Paszke; Sam Gross; Francisco Massa; A. Lerer

title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
abstract_600: We introduce Adam, an algorithm for first-order gradient-based optimization of stochastic objective functions, based on adaptive estimates of lower-order moments. The method is straightforward to implement, is computationally efficient, has little memory requirements, is invariant to diagonal rescaling of the gradients, and is well suited for problems that are large in terms of data and/or parameters. abstract_600: We note that common implementations of adaptive gradient algorithms, such as Adam, limit the potential benefit of weight decay regularization, because the weights do not decay multiplicatively (as would be expected for standard weight decay) but by an additive constant factor. title: SGDR: Stochastic Gradient Descent with Warm Restarts
abstract_600: Restart techniques are common in gradient-free optimization to deal with multimodal functions. Partial warm restarts are also gaining popularity in gradient-based optimization to improve the rate of convergence in accelerated gradient schemes to deal with ill-conditioned functions. In this paper, we propose a simple warm restart technique for stochastic gradient descent to improve its anytime performance when training deep neural networks. title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
authors: Kaiming He; X. Zhang; Shaoqing Ren; Jian Sun
abstract_600: Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, instead of learning unreferenced functions. title: Group Normalization
abstract_600: Batch Normalization (BN) is a milestone technique in the development of deep learning, enabling various networks to train. However, normalizing along the batch dimension introduces problems—BN’s error increases rapidly when the batch size becomes smaller, caused by inaccurate batch statistics estimation. This limits BN’s usage for training larger models and transferring features to computer vision tasks including detection, segmentation, and video, which require small batches constrained by memory consumption. title: Latent Denoising Diffusion GAN: Faster Sampling, Higher Image Quality

title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
authors: J. Redmon; S. Divvala; Ross B. Girshick; Ali Farhadi
abstract_600: We present YOLO, a new approach to object detection. Prior work on object detection repurposes classifiers to perform detection. Instead, we frame object detection as a regression problem to spatially separated bounding boxes and associated class probabilities. A single neural network predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities directly from full images in one evaluation.
